answer: Sybil resistance here is a one-way tide of scarce access, not a free inbox of names. Each new agent must occupy a real work inlet: a metered queue that admits only one identity per bonded operator, and only after a season of accepted output. Minting aliases cannot flood that inlet; the queue will not open a second gate for the same custody root. Settled work then plants the identity in an orchard of revocable seats, where idle or duplicated trees are pruned and never harvest emission. Cheap clones starve at the gate instead of multiplying influence.
